text:
Liam Delap came and went. He joined Chelsea in the summer of 2025 and was hailed by Enzo Maresca as the next Harry Kane. Fast forward a year, though, and there was no chance of Delap joining Kane in England’s World Cup squad. The striker’s form was miserable and the only surprise was that Chelsea made a profit when they sold him to Nottingham Forest for £50m last summer.
On one level it looks like good business. Delap’s only season at Stamford Bridge featured one serious hamstring injury, one league goal, one ridiculous red card and not much else. Analysts at other clubs rated him at Ipswich and felt Chelsea was the wrong fit for his direct style of play. The mistake was less the decision not to give Delap another season, no matter the worries over cover for João Pedro, more the call to sign him in the first place.
At the same time, however, Delap’s experience speaks to the questions around culture and identity dogging Chelsea before they face Forest and their former striker at the City Ground on Friday night. It is a point that could be applied to so many of the players to join during this ownership’s four years in charge. Alejandro Garnacho, languishing on loan at Aston Villa, was a £40m signing last year, and only three of the 12 players who joined in the 2024-25 season are still at the club.
There is a constant churn. Laurence Stewart has departed the five-strong sporting director team and there also are whispers around Dave Fallows, although insiders insist there will be no further changes. Back to the squad and Moisés Caicedo, Roméo Lavia and Cole Palmer are the only survivors from the 2023-24 intake. Wesley Fofana, Malo Gusto and Gaga Slonina remain from the 16 who joined in the 2022-23 season. The trading is relentless and, although the ability to raise funds meant Chelsea were in position to spend £117m on Morgan Rogers last summer, it is hard not to wonder whether the strategy has hindered the team’s development.
The lack of consistency was evident when Chelsea lost 4-1 at home to Leeds last Saturday. Xabi Alonso, whose side are eighth after five defeats in their first 11 league games, has focused on raising standards. But shifting mindset is harder when the players cannot fall back on a clear identity. The chopping and changing has consequences. Reece James, Chelsea’s captain, is the only first-teamer who represented the club during the Roman Abramovich era. It is not a surprise that supporters feel little connection to the players. Fans wonder whether the long contracts handed out to players have meaning. They hear Fofana appear to joke about missing a penalty against Liverpool and wonder whether the players care. It explains why the atmosphere at Stamford Bridge quickly grows toxic. The culture has to change. There has to be more accountability.
“This is a goal for us – that we are able to have stability, to be more competitive,” Alonso said on Thursday. “For me, to build that core, to build that way of doing things, it’s very important for the newcomers when you really get into the place and you know how things work.”
It is a work in progress. The final whistle against Leeds brought the sight of Palmer, who is horribly out of form, arguing with João Pedro and Willie Isa, the player support and development officer, about refusing to acknowledge the fans. There has been more woe this week, the mood soured by Fofana’s ill-advised chat with a French YouTuber. Fofana has had to apologise after failing to seek club permission for an interview in which he revealed that he almost quit football before his agents pointed out how much money was left on his contract.
Alonso, who refused to say whether the £75m defender had been fined, was unamused. “He apologised,” the manager said. “He knows it was not right. We are here to take things seriously.”
The worry is that Chelsea still look unserious. They have plenty to prove after being bullied by Leeds and Sunderland. Delap, who has been finetuning his heading in training this week, will fancy his chances after Fofana and Levi Colwill toiled against target men when they faced Leeds’ Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Sunderland’s Brian Brobbey.
Confidence in the defence is at rock bottom. Chelsea are not in Europe but Alonso is yet to feel the benefit of extra time on the training ground. His side have conceded 20 goals and keep making silly errors. Jamie Carragher, Alonso’s former teammate at Liverpool, destroyed the pairing of Fofana and Colwill on Sky Sports on this week’s Monday Night Football. They have been exposed by Maxence Lacroix’s hamstring injury. Alonso needs individuals to stop hiding. Chelsea’s midfield crumbled when Caicedo went off injured against Leeds, and the attack has spluttered without João Pedro.
There is no point crying about injuries. Chelsea have spent more than £1bn on their squad. Alonso, who accused his players of failing to perform the basics against Leeds, is yet to make sense of it all and has not instilled a playing identity. He talks about control but it is not clear what he wants Chelsea to be. It is Alonso’s puzzle to solve. Working it out will be easier if Chelsea finally develop some continuity.
digest_he: התקופה הקצרה של ליאם דלפ בצ'לסי, שהגיע בקול תרועה רמה בקיץ 2025 ונמכר זמן קצר לאחר מכן, מהווה סמל למדיניות התחלופה האגרסיבית של המועדון מאז חילופי הבעלות. מעבר השחקנים הסיטוני, שבו רק מעטים מהמצטרפים בשנים האחרונות נשארים לאורך זמן, פוגע אנושות בזהות הקבוצה ובחיבור שבין השחקנים לאוהדים. המאמן צ'אבי אלונסו מתמודד עם אתגר מורכב של בניית ליבה יציבה ושינוי מנטליות, במיוחד על רקע פציעות, יכולת דלה של שחקני מפתח ושערוריות משמעתיות מחוץ למגרש. למרות השקעות עתק בסגל, הקבוצה עדיין נראית חסרת כיוון ומשחקת ללא זהות ברורה, עובדה שמציבה סימני שאלה גדולים לגבי הצלחת האסטרטגיה של המועדון.
